messages:
sylvia: Automated alert: elevated p50/p95 latency for real-time-fallback (RTF) path in eu-west-2 starting ~11:12 UTC. Customers reporting slower responses.
drew: Looking—queue length up on rtf-pool, CPU on rtf nodes spiking. Any recent deploys to that pool?
omar: There was a small runtime patch to RTF rolled at 09:30 but no config changes. Could be traffic skew or a hot-process leak.
sylvia: Paging infra oncall and creating incident.
oncall-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-5991 created and assigned to infra-oncall. https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-5991
drew: Short-term mitigation: pin RTF traffic back to standard pooling for eu-west-2 to reduce pressure and prevent additional fallbacks.
omar: Applied routing change: smart-routing flag rtf.prefer=false for eu-west-2. Traffic rebalanced within ~90s.
status-bot: Status page updated: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/PD-5991 - "Increased latency on real-time fallback in EU-WEST-2; mitigation in progress."
drew: Also scaling the rtf pool and restarting a subset of nodes to drain hot processes. Command: kubectl scale deployment/rtf -n prod --replicas=8
omar: Scale and rolling restart applied. CPU usage trending down; p95 latency dropping from ~1.9s to ~0.4s.
cs: CS notified affected customers and posted an incident banner for impacted accounts.
sylvia: Follow-ups: 1) roll back or further inspect the 09:30 runtime patch 2) add autoscaling headroom alerts for RTF pools 3) add a canary test in deploy pipeline that exercises RTF under skewed traffic. Filing tickets INF-8300, INF-8301, INF-8302
oncall-bot: Incident PD-5991 status changed: mitigated -> monitoring
sylvia: Thanks team. Postmortem and customer timeline will be published in ~2h once root cause validated.
